name: PROCESS-based case-series checklist with aesthetic-medicine extensions
source_note: Domains follow the PROCESS guideline for surgical case series (Agha et al.; updated periodically — check the latest version at the official PROCESS site). Items are paraphrased and grouped; before submission download the official checklist the journal requires and transfer locations onto it. PROCESS is written for surgical series; for non-surgical aesthetic series it is the closest widely accepted reporting standard, and some journals accept CARE or STROBE instead — confirm with the target journal.

items.item: Includes 'case series' and the area of focus (intervention, complication, population).
aesthetic: State retrospective/prospective and single/multicentre in title or abstract.
items.ask: Is the series retrospective or prospective, and single-clinic or multi-clinic?

items.item: 3–6 keywords including 'case series'.
aesthetic: Material/device class and anatomical region.

items.item: Structured: introduction, methods, results, conclusion.
aesthetic: Report n, follow-up duration and the key effect estimate with 95% CI.

items.item: Background and rationale; relevant literature; what gap this series addresses.
aesthetic: Evidence to date for this indication/population (often industry-funded RCTs in Fitzpatrick I–III); why a local/real-world series adds value.
items.ask: What gap does this series fill (population, indication, technique, safety signal, long-term data)?

items.item: Aim/research question stated clearly.
items.ask: State the aim in one sentence (ideally PICOT-style).

items.item: Ethics approval (or exemption) and research registration where applicable; consent procedures.
aesthetic: Consent for publication of facial photographs.
Off-label use disclosed and approved.
items.ask: Ethics committee approval or exemption (name, number)? How was consent obtained, including for photographs?

items.item: Retrospective or prospective; single or multicentre; consecutive or non-consecutive inclusion.
aesthetic: For split-face designs: how the treated side was allocated (random, by patient preference, fixed).
items.ask: Were all eligible patients in the period included consecutively? For split-face, how was the side allocated?

items.item: Setting (type of clinic/hospital, geography) and dates of patient inclusion and follow-up.
aesthetic: For multi-clinic chains: number of sites and whether protocols were harmonised.
items.ask: Which clinics/sites, and the date range of treatment and follow-up?

items.item: Inclusion and exclusion criteria; how patients were identified.
aesthetic: Washout from prior treatments (e.g., fillers, toxin, energy devices) and prohibited concurrent treatments.
Fitzpatrick type distribution; BDD or unrealistic-expectation exclusion; pregnancy/lactation; weight stability.
items.ask: Inclusion/exclusion criteria? Required washout from previous treatments? How were patients identified (database search, clinic records)?

items.item: Patient optimisation or preparation before intervention.
aesthetic: Skin priming, barrier repair, antiviral prophylaxis, anticoagulant management, topical anaesthesia.

items.item: Full intervention details sufficient for replication.
aesthetic: Injectables: product, manufacturer, dose per area and total, dilution/reconstitution, plane, needle/cannula gauge, technique, sessions and intervals, touch-ups.
Devices: model, wavelength, fluence, pulse width, spot size, passes, cooling, endpoints.
Whether parameters varied between patients/sites and how.
items.ask: Standard protocol parameters, and how much did they vary between patients or clinics?

items.item: Who performed the intervention: number of operators, training, experience.
aesthetic: Years of injecting/device experience; whether a single operator or several (inter-operator variability).
items.ask: How many physicians performed the treatments, and their experience?

items.item: Outcome definitions, how and when measured; measures to ensure quality.
aesthetic: Standardised photography protocol (lighting, distance, views, camera/VISIA/3D).
Validated scales (GAIS, site-specific scales, FACE-Q); who rated and whether blinded; inter-rater agreement.
Responder definition specified in advance (e.g., GAIS 'improved' or ≥1-grade improvement).
items.ask: Primary outcome and how it was measured? Were photo ratings blinded and by how many raters? How was 'responder' defined?

items.item: Statistical methods, handling of missing data and loss to follow-up.
aesthetic: Paired tests for within-patient and split-face comparisons; non-parametric tests for ordinal scales; correction for multiple time points; CIs for rates (exact methods for small n).

items.item: Number screened/included, demographics and baseline characteristics; flow of patients.
aesthetic: Age, sex, Fitzpatrick type, baseline severity, prior treatments.

items.item: Actual intervention delivered and any deviations or changes, with reasons.
aesthetic: Total doses actually delivered (mean/median, range).
items.ask: Any deviations from the planned protocol (extra sessions, dose changes)?

items.item: Clinician- and patient-reported outcomes at each time point; length of follow-up; losses to follow-up.
aesthetic: Effect estimates with 95% CI, not p-values alone.
Duration of effect (e.g., Kaplan–Meier) when follow-up allows.
items.ask: How many patients were lost to follow-up at each visit, and why?

items.item: All complications/adverse events with timing, severity, management and outcome.
aesthetic: Event rates with exact 95% CI; when zero events, report the upper bound (rule of three).
items.ask: List every adverse event (including minor) with onset, management and resolution.

items.item: Adherence, tolerability, patient satisfaction.
aesthetic: Downtime, pain scores, satisfaction or FACE-Q.

items.item: Key findings in context of literature; strengths and limitations; relevance and implications.
aesthetic: Limitations: no control group, selection bias, unblinded ratings, industry products, confounders (weight change, concurrent skincare, season).

items.item: Conclusions supported by the data; future research directions.
aesthetic: Avoid causal or superiority claims a single-arm series cannot support.

items.item: Conflicts of interest, funding, product supply, AI-use disclosure.
aesthetic: Declare free product, speaker fees, or trainer roles with manufacturers.
items.ask: Any conflicts of interest, funding, or free product from manufacturers? Was AI used in preparing the manuscript (it was, via this workflow — confirm the disclosure wording)?

appraisal.name: JBI critical appraisal checklist for case series (self-check, paraphrased)
items: Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
Valid methods used to identify the condition for all participants?
Outcomes or follow-up results clearly reported?
Clear reporting of the presenting site/clinic demographic information?
